findings.claim: The new clause introduced 'the candidate' in the same instructions that elsewhere say 'the learner', naming one person by two terms a sentence apart.

A ~60-word parenthetical with an internal semicolon sat between the build sentence's object and the colon introducing the deliverable, obscuring the main clause and momentarily reading as requests reaching the app.
findings.recommendation: Split the API constraint into its own sentence and keep the build sentence short.

findings.claim: allowedResources still said 'the running practice API it names', readable as an already-running hosted service, contradicting the new candidate-local clause.
findings.recommendation: Align the resource entry: the local API its README names, started by the learner with the documented npm command.

items.note: No person is called 'the candidate' any more: the actor is 'the learner' in both the allowedResources entry and the constraint sentence; 'candidate-local' survives only as a compound adjective defined immediately in learner terms.

The parenthetical is out of the build sentence (now 'a provided candidate-local REST API'), the constraint stands as its own sentence, and 'a localhost address the app reads from the taught VITE_API_URL environment setting' removes the ambiguity. The added CORS clause is value-free, grammatical and within taught scope.

allowedResources now reads 'the local practice API its README names, started by the learner with the documented npm command' - no longer readable as an always-on hosted service and consistent with the candidate-local instructions.
